# Benchmark configuration

<!-- Generated by: python3 tools/bench_config.py --docs > docs/CONFIG.md (do not edit by hand) -->

A measurement is described by a short **measurement file** (`make run CONFIG=my.config`) that names a **machine profile**:

```
MACHINE=minimal
MEASURE=static
HTTP_REQUESTS=1000 20000 80000
```

Values come from the built-in defaults, then the machine profile (`configs/machine/<name>.config`), then the measurement file, which can override any setting. Every value actually used is written to `bench.config.resolved` in the results folder.

| Profile | For |
|---|---|
| `minimal` | A machine you control, left alone while it measures: CPU at a fixed speed, turbo off, other containers stopped, screen at 1%, keyboard light, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off |
| `tolerable` | As minimal, but Wi-Fi stays on (reached over the network, or must stay online) |
| `remote` | A machine you control over SSH (desktop, lab or university server): CPU fixed, turbo off, other containers stopped, nothing that could cut the connection; stops cleanly (resumable) after 15 minutes without calm |
| `cloud` | A rented machine: CPU settings where the provider allows them; shared hardware, so it measures after 10 minutes without calm and records why. Needs visible RAPL energy counters (bare-metal instances); the measurement stops at the start without them |
| `untouched` | A machine you must not change (shared with others, or no rights): nothing is changed; if it never becomes calm, it measures anyway and records why |

## Machine profile

### `MACHINE`

Default: `minimal`

How the machine is prepared: a profile in configs/machine/ (minimal, tolerable, remote, cloud, untouched) orthe path of a profile file. Any machine setting written in the measurement file overrides the profile. none = no profile, only the built-in defaults (which equal minimal).

Unit: profile name, .config file, or none

## What to measure

### `MEASURE`

Default: `static dynamic websocket concurrency payload`

Which kinds of measurement to run. static/dynamic: HTTP load levels (HTTP_REQUESTS) on the static and dynamic HTTP servers; websocket: burst and stream tests; concurrency and payload: the WebSocket client-count and message-size sweeps. A type on the command line (make run-static ...) takes precedence over this setting.

Unit: kinds, separated by spaces: static dynamic websocket concurrency payload

### `SERVERS`

Default: `(empty)`

Which servers to measure. Empty = every server found in BENCHMARKS_DIR (a folder with a Dockerfile; its place, static/, dynamic/ or websocket/, gives its type). A name is a server folder name, e.g. st-erlang-cowboy-28-4-3. An image built on this machine without a folder is given with its type: static:my-nginx, dynamic:my-app, websocket:my-ws (port from the image). Every name must exist and every image must be built, or the measurement does not start.

Unit: names separated by spaces, or empty = all servers found

### `VARIANTS`

Default: `(empty)`

Measure every selected server also with other container settings, in the same shuffled order. For each variant an image <server>-<NAME> is built at the start (the server's image plus these environment variables) and measured next to the server as it is. Example, BEAM scheduler busy-waiting off: nobw:ERL_FLAGS=+sbwt none +sbwtdcpu none +sbwtdio none. Empty = no variants.

Unit: NAME:VAR=value[|VAR=value], several separated by ;

### `BENCHMARKS_DIR`

Default: `(empty)`

The folder searched for servers. Empty = benchmarks/ (or BENCHMARKS_DIR from the environment). --bench on the command line takes precedence.

Unit: folder path, or empty = benchmarks/

## Machine settings (configs/machine/ profiles)

### `ENV_GOVERNOR`

Default: `performance`

CPU frequency governor during the measurement.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `performance` | CPU stays at its highest allowed frequency (steadiest, recommended) |
| `powersave` | CPU lowers its frequency when it can (Linux default on Intel laptops) |
| `schedutil` | frequency follows the load (only with some CPU drivers, e.g. AMD) |
| `ondemand` | frequency jumps up under load (only with some CPU drivers) |
| `conservative` | frequency rises slowly under load (only with some CPU drivers) |
| `unchanged` | leave the machine's current setting |

### `ENV_TURBO`

Default: `off`

Turbo boost: the CPU briefly running above its base frequency when it is cool enough.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `off` | no turbo; slower but much steadier results (recommended) |
| `on` | turbo allowed; faster, closer to everyday use, but more variation |
| `unchanged` | leave the machine's current setting |

### `ENV_STOP_CONTAINERS`

Default: `1`

Other Docker containers running during the measurement.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | stop them before, restart them after (recommended) |
| `0` | leave them running |

### `ENV_KEEP_CONTAINERS`

Default: `(empty)`

Containers that must keep running even when ENV_STOP_CONTAINERS=1.

Unit: container names, comma-separated, or empty

### `ENV_SCREEN_BRIGHTNESS`

Default: `1`

Screen brightness during the measurement (restored after). 1 = dimmest that is still on (0 switches the backlight off on some laptops, and a brightness key pressed then would change it mid-run). It does not change the container's energy (the screen is not part of the CPU), only the whole machine's. The desktop may still dim or switch off the screen by itself. Machines without a screen are not affected.

Unit: percent 0-100, or 'unchanged'

### `ENV_KEYBOARD_LIGHT`

Default: `off`

Keyboard backlight during the measurement.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `off` | switch it off, restored after (recommended) |
| `unchanged` | leave it as it is |

### `ENV_WIFI`

Default: `off`

Wi-Fi radio during the measurement. Off removes background network traffic and updates. The measurement needs no network. A run started over SSH through Wi-Fi refuses to switch it off (it would cut its own connection); set 'unchanged' there.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `off` | switch it off, restored after (recommended) |
| `unchanged` | leave it as it is |

### `ENV_BLUETOOTH`

Default: `off`

Bluetooth radio during the measurement.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `off` | switch it off, restored after (recommended) |
| `unchanged` | leave it as it is |

### `ON_BATTERY`

Default: `wait`

A laptop not on its charger: the CPU can run under other power limits on battery. Checked at the start and before every run; a run during which the charger was unplugged counts as failed. Machines without a battery are never affected.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `wait` | do not measure on battery; wait until the charger is back (recommended) |
| `stop` | stop the measurement; continue later with make resume |
| `ignore` | measure anyway |

### `SETTLE_SECONDS`

Default: `60`

Wait after applying the machine settings, before the resting state is measured.

Unit: seconds

### `RESTING_MEASURE_SECONDS`

Default: `10`

How long the resting temperature and CPU use are measured, after SETTLE_SECONDS. Longer = a more trustworthy resting value on a noisy machine. Used as the reference by the readiness checks.

Unit: seconds, 1 or more (one reading per second)

## Readiness check before every run (configs/machine/ profiles)

### `READY_CHECK_EVERY_SECONDS`

Default: `5`

While waiting for the machine to be ready, how often it is checked again.

Unit: seconds, 1 or more

### `READY_TEMP_REFERENCE_C`

Default: `(empty)`

Temperature the CPU is compared to. Empty = the resting temperature, measured automatically for RESTING_MEASURE_SECONDS (middle value of the readings). A number = use this fixed temperature.

Unit: degrees Celsius, or empty = measured automatically

### `READY_TEMP_MARGIN_C`

Default: `3`

Ready when CPU temperature <= READY_TEMP_REFERENCE_C + this margin. Examples: reference empty + margin 3 = back within 3 C of today's resting temperature; reference 50 + margin 0 = never start above 50 C. The sensor reads in steps of 1 C.

Unit: degrees Celsius, or empty = no temperature check

### `READY_CPU_BUSY_REFERENCE_PERCENT`

Default: `(empty)`

CPU use the whole machine is compared to. Empty = the resting CPU use, measured automatically (average over RESTING_MEASURE_SECONDS). A number = use this fixed value.

Unit: percent 0-100, or empty = measured automatically

### `READY_CPU_BUSY_MARGIN_PERCENT`

Default: `5`

Ready when whole-machine CPU use <= READY_CPU_BUSY_REFERENCE_PERCENT + this margin. Examples: reference empty + margin 5 = within 5% of the machine's resting use (shared machines); reference 0 + margin 5 = never start above 5% (your own quiet machine).

Unit: percent 0-100, or empty = no CPU check

### `READY_NO_THROTTLING`

Default: `1`

Thermal throttling: the CPU slowing itself down because it is too hot.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | not ready while the CPU is throttling (recommended) |
| `0` | ignore throttling |

### `READY_CONSECUTIVE_CHECKS`

Default: `2`

All checks must pass this many times in a row, so a short dip does not count.

Unit: checks, 1 or more

### `READY_MIN_WAIT_SECONDS`

Default: `10`

Always wait at least this long before a run, even if the machine already looks ready (lets the previous container stop and its connections close).

Unit: seconds

### `READY_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS`

Default: `300`

After this long without being ready, READY_ON_TIMEOUT decides what happens.

Unit: seconds, at least READY_MIN_WAIT_SECONDS

### `READY_ON_TIMEOUT`

Default: `wait`

What to do when the machine is still not ready after READY_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `wait` | keep waiting; never measure in a bad state; prints every minute what fails (recommended) |
| `stop` | stop the whole measurement with an error |
| `measure` | measure anyway and write the reason in the CSV (cloud or shared servers) |

## How much

### `REPEATS`

Default: `5`

How many times every measurement is repeated. Each repeat is one full pass over all servers.

Unit: runs, 1 or more

### `HTTP_REQUESTS`

Default: `100 1000 5000 8000 10000 15000 20000 30000 40000 50000 60000 70000 80000`

Load levels of the static and dynamic HTTP measurements, measured in this order.

Unit: request counts, separated by spaces

### `IDLE_SECONDS`

Default: `0`

Measure every server doing nothing for this long, right before its load. Gives its idle energy and power (Idle ... columns in the CSV). 0 = off, as in the published results. Adds this many seconds to every measurement.

Unit: seconds, 0 = off

### `WARMUP_SECONDS`

Default: `0`

Unmeasured traffic of the same kind as the load (HTTP requests or WebSocket echo messages) for this long after the server starts, so the measurement does not include its very first requests. The readiness check afterwards lets the CPU cool down again. 0 = off, as in the published results.

Unit: seconds, 0 = off

## Failures and raw data

### `FAILURES_STOP_AFTER`

Default: `5`

What to do when a measurement fails (server did not start, health check failed, ...). Every failure is written to failures.csv.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | stop at the first failure |
| `N` | keep going, but stop after N failures in a row, because then something is broken (default 5) |
| `0` | never stop; measure everything that works |

### `RAW_DATA`

Default: `keep`

Scaphandre's raw power log of each run, after its energy has been calculated.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `keep` | keep it as it is (plain JSON) in <results>/raw/ (energy can be recalculated later; recommended) |
| `delete` | delete it (saves disk space) |

## Order of the runs

### `SHUFFLE`

Default: `1`

Shuffle the order of the servers in every repeat, so no server always runs first on a cool machine.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | shuffle (recommended) |
| `0` | same order in every repeat |

### `SHUFFLE_SEED`

Default: `(empty)`

Number that decides the shuffled order. Empty = random; the number used is saved in metadata.json and schedule.txt. Put it here to rerun exactly the same order (same servers).

Unit: whole number, or empty

## Load and energy measurement

### `HTTP_MAX_WORKERS`

Default: `100`

How many requests the HTTP client sends in parallel. 'system' = Python's default (differs per machine).

Unit: threads, 1 or more, or 'system'

### `HTTP_CONNECTION`

Default: `reuse`

How the HTTP client uses TCP connections.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reuse` | one kept-alive connection per worker, like browsers (recommended) |
| `per-request` | a new connection for every request, as in the published results; fails above ~28,000 requests when the client runs out of ports |

### `SCAPH_STEP_MS`

Default: `500`

How often Scaphandre reads the power. Smaller = more detail but Scaphandre itself uses more power.

Unit: milliseconds, 10 or more

## WebSocket workloads (full runs; --quick and --super-quick keep their short lists)

### `WS_BURST_CLIENTS`

Default: `5 50 100`

WebSocket burst: how many clients connect at once.

Unit: client counts, separated by spaces

### `WS_BURST_SIZES_KB`

Default: `8 1024 65536`

WebSocket burst: message sizes.

Unit: KB per message, separated by spaces

### `WS_BURST_BURSTS`

Default: `3`

WebSocket burst: how many bursts each client sends.

Unit: bursts per client, separated by spaces

### `WS_BURST_INTERVAL_SECONDS`

Default: `0.5`

Pause between bursts, also used by the concurrency and payload tests. 0.5 = as in the published results; 0 = back-to-back bursts (as fast as possible, like the Green Metrics Tool).

Unit: seconds, 0 or more

### `WS_STREAM_CLIENTS`

Default: `5 50 100`

WebSocket stream: how many clients send at the same time.

Unit: client counts, separated by spaces

### `WS_STREAM_SIZES_KB`

Default: `8 1024 65536`

WebSocket stream: message sizes.

Unit: KB per message, separated by spaces

### `WS_STREAM_RATE_PER_SECOND`

Default: `10`

WebSocket stream: sending rate.

Unit: messages per second per client, separated by spaces

### `WS_STREAM_DURATION_SECONDS`

Default: `5`

WebSocket stream: how long each client sends.

Unit: seconds, separated by spaces

### `WS_CONCURRENCY_CLIENTS`

Default: `100 1000 5000`

WebSocket concurrency test: numbers of simultaneous clients.

Unit: client counts, separated by spaces

### `WS_CONCURRENCY_SIZE_KB`

Default: `8`

WebSocket concurrency test: message size.

Unit: KB per message

### `WS_PAYLOAD_CLIENTS`

Default: `5`

WebSocket payload test: number of clients.

Unit: clients

### `WS_PAYLOAD_SIZES_KB`

Default: `8 1024 65536`

WebSocket payload test: message sizes.

Unit: KB per message, separated by spaces
